claims.text: POL-RD-01 is satisfied on the trace figure. The GPS polyline between the recorded pickup event (06:30:55) and the recorded dropoff event (06:49:35) measures 14.37 km against a platform optimal of 11.0 km, an excess of 3.37 km, or 30.64% of optimal. Both establishment limbs pass: 30.64% is greater than the 20% threshold and 3.37 km is greater than the 0.8 km threshold. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED. Per POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs, and trip_record.actual_distance_km (14.4 km) is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. EV-GPS-03108 carries 113 fixes at a 10 second sample interval over 100.0% coverage, with max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps array; there is no gap above 90 seconds between consecutive fixes, no straight-line jump above 500 m, and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. Limbs (a) to (c) do not fire, so the excess stands on the trace itself, no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. (a) The artifacts describe the same trip: EV-TRIP-03108, EV-GPS-03108 and EV-FARE-03108 all carry trip_id TRP-03108, and the trip_record start 06:30:55 matches the first GPS fix at 06:30:55. (b) The excess of 3.37 km / 30.64% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold and is measured from a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; his counterparty statement names no artifact and no clause and does not discharge it.

The extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not triggered on this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-or-more figure the clause requires before a sub-30%-excess claim needs corroboration beyond the trace, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. Those two fields are cited only for the test POL-RD-08 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires; nothing else on the rider profile bears on the outcome of this claim.

The driver's traffic explanation fails on the record. His statement says only that 'traffic was heavy so I took another road', and the bundle contains no traffic_advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-03108-01 has admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window'). I disclose that impairment and that zero weight expressly. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries an overlapping validity window, and is matched by a route that leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after; with no advisory on file that comparison cannot be run, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the excuse is a general traffic assertion, which POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the driver's burden.

With no traffic_advisory on file, POL-RD-13 governs and the deviation stands at the measured figure. The driver named no evidence ID for any advisory, so under POL-RD-13(1) the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The consequence under POL-RD-13(2) is that the driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour is on file, so no distance is excluded under POL-RD-04. The chat log holds exactly one message, and it identifies no road and carries waypoint_hint null, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 cannot be run; where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named, the clause is unavailable on the record and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The trace in any event runs continuously from 06:30:55 to 06:49:35 with no gap, and nothing in it follows a rider-named waypoint, so POL-RD-14 does not engage POL-RD-10(7) either.

The single chat message cannot be read as the rider accepting the route or waiving the claim. EV-CHAT-03108's own sender field attributes MSG-03108-001 to DRIVER, not to the rider and not to the platform, even though its text is dressed as a '[Ryde System Notice]' and asserts a waiver (WAIVER-2231) that no artifact in the bundle evidences. POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider; this one does not. It also fails POL-RD-04(b) and (c), naming no road and carrying no waypoint_hint. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence ID beyond itself carries no weight, so a driver-authored message cannot supply the rider instruction the clause requires, and nothing in it alters the arithmetic refund.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, under POL-RD-02, and this trip's fare_model is METERED. From EV-FARE-03108: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 14.9) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting-time fee - 0 promo = 17.0220. charged_total is 20.64, so the refund is 3.6180 - above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and 17.5% of charged_total, far short of the 90% full-refund share. The payable figure rounds UP to SGD 3.65. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-03108, where it is 1.0.

The correct remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial, not a full refund: the excess of 30.64% is below POL-RD-01's 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation, POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and no POL-RD-06(b) uplift arises. The driver's profile confirms no pattern in any event - deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 231 - so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is sought either. The rider asks only for the 3.65 the policy computes.

The present state is a charge, so the rider's relief has to come from the ruling. EV-FARE-03108 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and this dispute is rider-filed. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would preserve that state and leave the rider carrying the whole 20.64, while a PARTIAL_REFUND is what actually returns money; the amount contested is 3.00 and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic yields 3.65, so the rider seeks the computed figure, which covers the contested amount in full. The fare carries zero ERP lines and zero airport surcharge, so nothing needs to be added on top for pass-through lines under POL-RD-09.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this should be ruled rather than escalated. The identifiers match across EV-TRIP-03108, EV-GPS-03108 and EV-FARE-03108 (all TRP-03108); the pickup and dropoff timestamps on the admitted artifacts agree to within seconds; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); every charge line has a counterpart (no ERP gantries, no surcharge); and the refund of 3.6180 is far below the SGD 150.00 and charged_total ceilings. Escalation here would hold the rider's money for no reason the policy names.

claims.text: The excess on the governing trace figure is 3.37 km and 30.64% of the 11.0 km optimal route — over the POL-RD-01 establishment gate, but far under the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate. This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so the rider cannot reach the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b), and the case is capped at the arithmetic partial refund of POL-RD-02.

The refund is arithmetic and it is small. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare against the booked optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.0 km + 0.28 x 14.9 min) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown = 16.222, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 17.022. The refund is 20.64 - 17.022 = 3.618, rounded up to SGD 3.65 — only 17.5% of the charged total, nowhere near the 90% share that would license FULL_REFUND. The $20.64 the rider quotes is the metered fare for the trip as driven, not the rider's loss.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP charge (0.00 on and off the optimal route), no toll and no airport surcharge, no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, and the trip neither originated nor ended at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore makes no pass-through correction, and limb (1) of that clause forbids adding off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 refund in any event.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built on this driver from the only fields the clause allows: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 231, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more over at least 40 trips) is met. With no pattern established, and the deviation not material, there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral.

The driver's explanation that heavy traffic forced another road cannot be run on this record, and the driver does not press it as an exoneration. EV-ADVIS-03108-01 is a MISSING artifact — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no advisory covering the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window — so the POL-RD-03 advisory test cannot be performed, and under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion of bad traffic discharges nothing. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight, reduces no excess and supplies no amended optimal, so the deviation stands at the 3.37 km measured against the booked 11.0 km optimal.

The sole chat message on this trip (MSG-03108-001, sent 06:35:55) was sent by the DRIVER, not the rider, and its waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on and that the trace corroborates within 200 m, so that clause cannot be met and no distance is excluded on a rider-requested detour; the driver does not rely on that message as an exoneration.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the route deviation is established but modest, and a partial refund of SGD 3.65 is due to the rider. This ruling is provisional and may be appealed within 30 days under POL-GEN-04; its monetary effect (SGD 3.65) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue.

1. Deviation (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace EV-GPS-03108 measures 14.37 km between the recorded pickup (06:30:55) and dropoff (06:49:35); the platform's optimal route on the trip record EV-TRIP-03108 is 11.0 km. The excess is 3.37 km, or 30.64% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. It is not MATERIAL: 30.64% is below 50% and 3.37 km is below 8.0 km. Per POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs and the rounded 14.4 km on the trip record is not used for the threshold.

2. Trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace is not impaired: 113 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, max gap 0.0 s, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained interval over 30 seconds. No independent corroboration is therefore required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

3. The driver's traffic explanation (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08, POL-RD-13). The driver's statement that 'traffic was heavy so I took another road' names no road and cites no advisory. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03108-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it covers no corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against that advisory and nothing else, the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 the uncited assertion carries no weight and reduces no excess. The deviation therefore stands at the measured 3.37 km against the booked 11.0 km optimal.

4. Rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14). The single chat message (EV-CHAT-03108, MSG-03108-001) is attributed by the log's own sender field to the DRIVER, not the rider. Its '[Ryde System Notice]' styling and the waiver it asserts (WAIVER-2231) are supported by no artifact. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider, and this is not one; its waypoint_hint is null and it names no road in any event. No distance is excluded, the message cannot be read as a rider waiver or acceptance, and POL-RD-14 does not engage POL-RD-10(7) because there is no rider instruction at all.

5. Refund (POL-RD-02). The fare model is METERED. Recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.0 km + 0.28 x 14.9 min) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier being read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-03108 = 16.222, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 17.0220. Charged total is 20.64. Refund = 20.64 - 17.0220 = 3.6180, above the 0.50 de minimis floor, rounded UP to SGD 3.65. That is 17.5% of the charged total, far short of the 90% that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

6. Pass-through lines (POL-RD-09). The fare carries no ERP charge (0.00 on and off the optimal route), no toll and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originated nor ended at an airport. Nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and limb (1) of the clause forbids adding off-route ERP in any event.

7. No repeat-pattern uplift or conduct referral (POL-RD-06). POL-RD-06 is consulted only on a MATERIAL deviation or finely balanced evidence; this deviation is not material. In any case the driver profile shows driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d = 231, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) arises and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is made. No other profile field is used, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

8. Escalation. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match across trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown (all TRP-03108); the trace is unimpaired; the timestamps agree; the refund of 3.65 is far below both the SGD 150.00 and charged_total ceilings; and no charge line is unmatched. The case is ruled, not escalated.

9. Discarded material. Two rider claims were discarded at the mechanical stage for citing the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-03108-01 without naming its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires; their substance (that the driver's traffic excuse cannot run and that no escalation trigger fires) is carried by the surviving claims of both sides and is reflected above. One open question is left to the human queue rather than the referrals list: MSG-03108-001 is a driver-authored message dressed as a platform system notice asserting a rider waiver that no artifact supports. To both parties: the rider is refunded SGD 3.65, and the rest of the SGD 20.64 fare stands. Both sides' surviving claims are accepted; the parties largely agree on the arithmetic and differ only on the driver's traffic explanation and on the single chat message, and both of those fail on the record.

1. The deviation is established (POL-RD-01). Measured on the governing artifact, the GPS trace, the polyline between the recorded pickup (06:30:55) and dropoff (06:49:35) is 14.37 km against a booked optimal route of 11.0 km — an excess of 3.37 km, or 30.64% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km). As POL-RD-01 requires, the trace figure governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km (14.4 km) was not used for the threshold test. The deviation is not MATERIAL: 30.64% is under the 50% gate and 3.37 km is under the 8.0 km gate, so the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is not available to the rider.

2. The trace is clean (POL-RD-07). EV-GPS-03108 carries 113 fixes at a 10-second interval over 100.0% coverage, with a maximum gap of 0.0 s and an empty gaps array: no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sampling interval over 30 seconds. Limbs (a)-(c) do not fire, so the excess stands on the trace itself, no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

3. The driver's traffic explanation reduces nothing (POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08, POL-RD-13). The bundle holds no advisory for this window: EV-ADVIS-03108-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the driver's statement names no evidence ID at all. The advisory test in POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run and that clause is unavailable; under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence carries no weight, and under POL-RD-13 a traffic excuse is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, that it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and that POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route. Because no party cited the missing advisory as an exoneration, this is not the POL-RD-10(5) escalation of an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and no escalation follows.

4. No rider-requested detour excludes any distance (POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14). The chat log holds one message only, and the log's own sender field attributes MSG-03108-001 to the DRIVER, with waypoint_hint null and no road named. POL-RD-04(a)-(c) is not met, so the clause is unavailable and no distance is excluded; POL-RD-14 confirms this is a failed exoneration rather than the contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes.

5. The driver's chat message is rejected and has no effect on the fare. It presents itself as a '[Ryde System Notice]' saying the rider accepted the longer route and waived any claim (WAIVER-2231), but the log attributes it to the driver and no artifact evidences any such waiver. No clause gives a message of that kind any effect, it is not a rider instruction under POL-RD-04(a) and, under POL-RD-08, it carries no weight. The rider is not bound by it, and it changes neither the excess nor the refund.

- charged_total: SGD 20.64
- recomputed_fare: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.0 km + 0.28 x 14.9 min) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting-time fee - 0 promo = SGD 17.0220
- refund: 20.64 - 17.0220 = SGD 3.6180, rounded up to SGD 3.65
The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 17.5% of charged_total, far short of the 90% that would make it a full refund. The rider's filed figure of SGD 3.00 was an estimate; the policy arithmetic governs and yields SGD 3.65, which covers the contested amount.

7. Nothing is added on top (POL-RD-09). The fare carries no ERP charge, no toll and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither began nor ended at an airport, so there is no pass-through correction; limb (1) also forbids adding off-route ERP to the POL-RD-02 figure.

8. No repeat-deviation pattern and no referral (POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01). On the only fields the clause allows, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 231, so neither limb of the pattern test is met. With no pattern established and the deviation not material, there is no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The rider's fields (deviation_claims_60d 1, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0) are below the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger and do not change the outcome; all other profile fields are context only and were not used.

9. No escalation. Identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown (all TRP-03108), the timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, every charge line has a counterpart, and the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires, so the case is ruled rather than held.

The monetary effect of SGD 3.65 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it is executed automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route. As a closing note, and not as a referral, the driver-authored chat message dressed as a system notice and an unsupported waiver is a matter a human reviewer may wish to look at separately; it has no bearing on the money in this ruling.

The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; his counterparty statement names no artifact and no clause and does not discharge it.

The extra-corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not triggered on this rider. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-or-more figure the clause requires before a sub-30%-excess claim needs corroboration beyond the trace, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. Those two fields are cited only for the test POL-RD-08 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires; nothing else on the rider profile bears on the outcome of this claim.

The driver's traffic explanation fails on the record. His statement says only that 'traffic was heavy so I took another road', and the bundle contains no traffic_advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-03108-01 has admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window'). I disclose that impairment and that zero weight expressly. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries an overlapping validity window, and is matched by a route that leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after; with no advisory on file that comparison cannot be run, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the excuse is a general traffic assertion, which POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the driver's burden.

With no traffic_advisory on file, POL-RD-13 governs and the deviation stands at the measured figure. The driver named no evidence ID for any advisory, so under POL-RD-13(1) the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The consequence under POL-RD-13(2) is that the driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-03108-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: No rider-requested detour is on file, so no distance is excluded under POL-RD-04. The chat log holds exactly one message, and it identifies no road and carries waypoint_hint null, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 cannot be run; where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named, the clause is unavailable on the record and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The trace in any event runs continuously from 06:30:55 to 06:49:35 with no gap, and nothing in it follows a rider-named waypoint, so POL-RD-14 does not engage POL-RD-10(7) either.

The single chat message cannot be read as the rider accepting the route or waiving the claim. EV-CHAT-03108's own sender field attributes MSG-03108-001 to DRIVER, not to the rider and not to the platform, even though its text is dressed as a '[Ryde System Notice]' and asserts a waiver (WAIVER-2231) that no artifact in the bundle evidences. POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider; this one does not. It also fails POL-RD-04(b) and (c), naming no road and carrying no waypoint_hint. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence ID beyond itself carries no weight, so a driver-authored message cannot supply the rider instruction the clause requires, and nothing in it alters the arithmetic refund.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, under POL-RD-02, and this trip's fare_model is METERED. From EV-FARE-03108: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 14.9) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting-time fee - 0 promo = 17.0220. charged_total is 20.64, so the refund is 3.6180 - above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and 17.5% of charged_total, far short of the 90% full-refund share. The payable figure rounds UP to SGD 3.65. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-03108, where it is 1.0.

The correct remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial, not a full refund: the excess of 30.64% is below POL-RD-01's 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation, POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and no POL-RD-06(b) uplift arises. The driver's profile confirms no pattern in any event - deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 231 - so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is sought either. The rider asks only for the 3.65 the policy computes.

The present state is a charge, so the rider's relief has to come from the ruling. EV-FARE-03108 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and this dispute is rider-filed. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would preserve that state and leave the rider carrying the whole 20.64, while a PARTIAL_REFUND is what actually returns money; the amount contested is 3.00 and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic yields 3.65, so the rider seeks the computed figure, which covers the contested amount in full. The fare carries zero ERP lines and zero airport surcharge, so nothing needs to be added on top for pass-through lines under POL-RD-09.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this should be ruled rather than escalated. The identifiers match across EV-TRIP-03108, EV-GPS-03108 and EV-FARE-03108 (all TRP-03108); the pickup and dropoff timestamps on the admitted artifacts agree to within seconds; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); every charge line has a counterpart (no ERP gantries, no surcharge); and the refund of 3.6180 is far below the SGD 150.00 and charged_total ceilings. Escalation here would hold the rider's money for no reason the policy names.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-03108-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: The excess on the governing trace figure is 3.37 km and 30.64% of the 11.0 km optimal route — over the POL-RD-01 establishment gate, but far under the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate. This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so the rider cannot reach the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b), and the case is capped at the arithmetic partial refund of POL-RD-02.

The refund is arithmetic and it is small. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare against the booked optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 11.0 km + 0.28 x 14.9 min) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown = 16.222, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 17.022. The refund is 20.64 - 17.022 = 3.618, rounded up to SGD 3.65 — only 17.5% of the charged total, nowhere near the 90% share that would license FULL_REFUND. The $20.64 the rider quotes is the metered fare for the trip as driven, not the rider's loss.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP charge (0.00 on and off the optimal route), no toll and no airport surcharge, no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, and the trip neither originated nor ended at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore makes no pass-through correction, and limb (1) of that clause forbids adding off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 refund in any event.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built on this driver from the only fields the clause allows: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 231, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more over at least 40 trips) is met. With no pattern established, and the deviation not material, there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral.

The driver's explanation that heavy traffic forced another road cannot be run on this record, and the driver does not press it as an exoneration. EV-ADVIS-03108-01 is a MISSING artifact — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no advisory covering the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window — so the POL-RD-03 advisory test cannot be performed, and under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion of bad traffic discharges nothing. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight, reduces no excess and supplies no amended optimal, so the deviation stands at the 3.37 km measured against the booked 11.0 km optimal.

The sole chat message on this trip (MSG-03108-001, sent 06:35:55) was sent by the DRIVER, not the rider, and its waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on and that the trace corroborates within 200 m, so that clause cannot be met and no distance is excluded on a rider-requested detour; the driver does not rely on that message as an exoneration.
